2. Facts relevant for disposal of the instant Rule are that on 19-6-2005 the predecessor of the opposite-party No. 1 as pre-emptor filed an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 being Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2005 before the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Bagharpara, Jessore for pre-empting the case land measuring 5 decimals appertaining to SA Khatian No. 39, Plot No. 626 (old), and No. 951 (present) of Mouza Dogachhia under Police Station Bagharpara, District Jessore. 

 4. The case of the pre-emptee-petitioner is that without cause of action the case is bad for defect of parties, barred by limitation and the case land along with other lands originally belonged to three brothers, namely Bhejal Mondal, Sharat Mondal and Bharat Mondal in equal shares and SA Khatian No. 34 was correctly prepared and finally published in their names. Bhejal Mondal died leaving behind one daughter named Laxibala Bhoumik as his sole heir. Thereafter Bharat Mondal died behind his brother Sharat Mondal to succeed his estate and then Sharat Mondal died leaving behind his widow and the preemptee as his heirs. Out of necessity for money, the mother of the pre-emptee mortgaged 37 decimals of land from the case jote to Amullya Sarker and Bijoy Krishna Sarker by a registered deed of patta and subsequently, SA record was prepared in the name of the said Amullya Sarker and Bijoy Krishna Sarker. Although the mortgage money was repaid, a redemption deed could not be executed due to financial crisis of the pre-emptee and his mother. The SA Khatian prepared and published in the name of Amullya Sarker and Bijoy Krishna Sarker is erroneous and the pre-emptee had no knowledge about the said khatian. The pre-emptee is in possession of 49 decimals of land in the case jote by inheritance and as such he is a co-sharer in the same. The pre-emptor had full knowledge about the impugned sale and that he has no necessity to pre-empt the case land and thereof, the application for pre-emption is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The pre-emptor examined 2 P.W.s including himself as PW 1 and the pre-emptee cross-examined them in detail. The pre-emptor exhibited the impugned sale deed dated 2-6-2005, SA Khatian No. 39 and the sale deed dated 22-1-1995 as Exhibits 1, 2 and 3 respectively. Although the examination-in-chief of the pre-emptee as OPW 1 was recorded in part, he did not turn up before the trial Court to complete his remaining examination-in-chief, the cross-examination and accordingly, no other documentary evidence was produced by him to substantiate his defence case as contended in his written objection.
